Fourth-quarter revenue will be $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, the chipmaker said in a statement Tuesday. That easily topped the average analyst estimate of $16.3 billion, helping send the shares up about 7% in late trading. 
  November 04, 2026 / 06:34 IST  
Advanced Micro Devices Inc., a key challenger to Nvidia Corp. in artificial intelligence chips, gave a sales forecast that soared past analysts’ projections, a sign of buoyant demand for data center processors.
The outlook provided fresh evidence that AI spending is sustainable, soothing jittery investors. Shares of chipmakers and other tech companies have been battered in recent weeks over concerns about a bubble in the AI infrastructure industry.
“AMD’s earnings are simultaneously a test of its own performance and of the broader AI trade,” Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne said in a note. The results “will give investors encouragement given the recent tech and semiconductor selloff, as investors increasingly scrutinize AI spending and its returns.”
AMD’s outlook — along with a strong forecast from server maker Super Micro Computer Inc. — helped spark a late-trading rally among AI equipment makers and cloud providers. Shares of companies from CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV to Dell Technologies Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. all gained.
Under Chief Executive Officer Lisa Su, AMD has become one of the most important suppliers of processors and computers that operate at the heart of AI facilities, underpinning a flood of new services.
Even with recent market turbulence, AMD shares have more than doubled this year. The company’s valuation reached $1 trillion in September, putting it in an elite group.
The data center growth has helped AMD offset a slump in the personal computer market, where rising memory-chip costs have slowed production and depressed user demand. Intel Corp., AMD’s top rival in that field, suffered its worst stock decline in decades after a downbeat earnings report last week.
One possible weak spot for AMD: Its gross margin will narrow to about 55% in the fourth quarter. That measure — the percentage of sales after removing production costs — had been 56% in the previous period.
On a conference call with anlysts, Su said the company has become more optimistic about long-term growth. It expects revenue to increase more than 80% next year, outpacing the 75% expansion seen by Wall Street. Sales from data centers will more than double, accounting for as much as 80% of total revenue.
The company “has strong confidence in our ability to sustain exceptional revenue growth for years to come, with earnings growing even faster,” Su said.
AMD’s third-quarter sales rose 45% to $13.4 billion. Profit climbed to $2.09 a share, minus certain items. Analysts on average had predicted revenue of $13.1 billion and earnings of $1.97 a share.
AMD continues to deliver record results and now boasts sales that are twice as big as they were two years ago. It’s also been outperforming longtime nemesis Intel in the market for central processing units, or CPUs. But the company is still well behind Nvidia in so-called AI accelerators, which are used to train and run artificial intelligence models.
Sales at AMD’s data center business nearly doubled to $8.5 billion. Analysts had predicted a total of $8.2 billion. PC and gaming-related sales shrank 8% to $3.7 billion.
Like other makers of components for PCs, AMD is suffering from a side effect of the data center boom. AI servers require a massive amount of memory. That’s cut into the supply of chips available for laptops and desktop machines — and forced prices up. The total PC market will decline by a double-digit percentage next year, Su said during the conference call.
AMD is debuting new product ranges in both the CPU and accelerator markets. The Santa Clara, California-based company is also taking on Nvidia more directly with its Helios server design.
But Nvidia, the largest chipmaker and world’s most valuable company, hasn’t been standing still. It’s updating its own lineup at a fast pace and branching out into everything from software to networking to complete computers.

Sun Pharma Gets Approval For Semaglutide Pill In India: How Will This Impact Diabetes Treatment?
The pill's active ingredient (raw material) will be sourced from China's Hangzhou-province-based Zhongmeihuadong Pharmaceutical.
India's pharmaceutical giant, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited, has secured regulatory approval from India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to manufacture and market a once-daily generic oral semaglutide tablet in India. The once-daily oral pill has been specifically approved for the treatment of Type-2 diabetes to improve glycaemic control. The drug is therapeutically equivalent to Novo Nordisk's innovator drug, Rybelsus.
According to an ET Pharma report, it has been approved in three standard oral dosage strengths: 3 mg, 7 mg, and 14 mg. The formulation uses a recombinant DNA (r-DNA) origin product and will be produced at Sun Pharma's manufacturing unit located in Kamrup, Assam, India.
The ET report has also mentioned that the pill's active ingredient (raw material) will be sourced from China's Hangzhou-province-based Zhongmeihuadong Pharmaceutical.
The patent for semaglutide expired early in 2026. Torrent Pharma was the first Indian manufacturer to launch generic oral semaglutide under brand names Semalix and Sembolic and held a dominant market share in oral generics prior to Sun Pharma's entry. Dr. Reddy's Laboratories also markets generic oral semaglutide - Obeda.
Sun Pharma previously received approval and launched injectable semaglutide formulations in India: Sematrinity (for Type 2 diabetes) and Noveltreat (for chronic weight management).
Adding the daily oral tablet gives Sun Pharma a complete GLP-1 therapy portfolio across both oral and injectable routes.
While Sun Pharma's retail price is unannounced, Dr. Reddy's Obeda is priced at Rs 99, Rs 135 and Rs 225 for the 3 mg, 7 mg, and 14 mg strengths, respectively.
The entry of oral semaglutide into the Indian market marks a significant shift in how Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and associated metabolic conditions are managed in India.
Oral semaglutide, like Novo Nordisk's Rybelsus, carried a high price point, limiting its use primarily to upper-middle-class urban populations. Domestic manufacturing by Sun Pharma, alongside existing generic makers like Torrent Pharma and Dr. Reddy's, drives significant price competition, making GLP-1 therapy dramatically more affordable.
A daily pill makes it easier to start treatment without the need for needles or complicated storage. This encourages patients to begin therapy earlier in their disease and stick to taking their medication every day.
India has a high rate of Type 2 diabetes, often called the "diabetes capital of the world." Many people develop this condition early in life due to issues like obesity and metabolic syndrome.
Oral semaglutide not only lowers HbA1c levels substantially but also promotes weight loss by delaying gastric emptying and increasing satiety. This addresses a core driver of insulin resistance.

White-collar hiring grows 14% in Oct, led by manufacturing
India's white-collar hiring surged 14% in October, driven by manufacturing demand. Naukri JobSpeak Index shows growth across metros & smaller cities.
Key Points
- White-collar hiring in India increased by 14% year-on-year in October.
- The manufacturing sector was the primary driver, with a 39% growth in production and manufacturing roles.
- The Naukri JobSpeak Index climbed to 2,836 in October, reflecting recruitment trends.
- Hyderabad led metro cities in contribution, while Gandhinagar showed the fastest growth among smaller cities.
- Demand for AI skills remains strong, indicating selective, fundamentals-led hiring.
The Naukri JobSpeak Index, which measures recruitment trends, climbed to 2,836 in October from 2,480 in the same month last year.
Across industries, hiring for production and manufacturing functions grew 39 per cent, making it one of the fastest-rising job functions, the report stated.
"Some of October's growth reflects last year's festive-season base, and we should read it in that light. What's encouraging is the kind of hiring we're seeing. Manufacturing companies are building capacity, and demand for AI skills remains strong, indicative of the selective, fundamentals-led nature of hiring demand," Info Edge (India) Limited MD and CEO Hitesh Oberoi said.
The Naukri JobSpeak report is based on a monthly index that tracks trends in India's job market and hiring activity, based on new job postings (including free job listings) and recruiter searches on naukri.com's resume database.
Among metro cities, the report revealed that Hyderabad led with the maximum contribution at 15 per cent, followed by Pune (14 per cent) and Delhi NCR (13 per cent).
Jobs in Bengaluru and Mumbai grew 12 per cent each. Chennai saw a growth of 11 per cent and the pace remained unchanged in Kolkata.
The fastest growth came from smaller cities, including Gandhinagar at 48 per cent, Surat 36 per cent, Vadodara 30 per cent and Ahmedabad 23 per cent, giving the state four of the seven fastest-growing emerging cities.
Other cities on the list included Raipur (34 per cent), Ranchi (29 per cent) and Jaipur (26 per cent), the report said.

work-careers-5612d079b0.headline: India's white-collar hiring rises 14% in October, manufacturing leads with 39% growth: Report
work-careers-5612d079b0.fulltext:
New Delhi [India], November 3 (ANI): Production and manufacturing roles led India's white-collar recruitment activity in October, with total hiring expanding 14 per cent year-on-year (YoY), according to the latest Naukri JobSpeak report. The auto sector led the sectoral expansion with a 36 per cent rise, supported by strong gains across core industrial operations, while the overall index climbed to 2,836 compared to 2,480 recorded in October 2025.
The higher YoY jump received support from a soft comparative festive base, as Diwali occurred in October last year and suppressed recruitment during those holiday periods. Across industries, production and manufacturing functions grew 39 per cent. Sectoral figures showed BPO and ITES expanding 17 per cent, followed by Banking and Financial Services at 16 per cent.
Hitesh Oberoi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Info Edge (India) Limited, said, "Some of October’s growth reflects last year’s festive-season base, and we should read it in that light. What’s encouraging is the kind of hiring we’re seeing. Manufacturing companies are building capacity, and demand for AI skills remains strong, indicative of the selective, fundamentals-led nature of hiring demand."
The auto industry reflected this operational focus prominently. Research and development recruitment in auto rose 53 per cent, procurement and supply chain grew 50 per cent, and production and manufacturing roles advanced 41 per cent. In contrast, auto sales and business development hiring increased by 7 per cent.
Similar patterns emerged in heavy machinery, where production roles rose 40 per cent and quality assurance grew 41 per cent. In the construction, engineering, cement, and metals sector, production jobs increased 33 per cent, project and programme management grew 25 per cent, and site engineering rose 20 per cent. 
While FMCG grew 6 per cent overall, its production hiring jumped 40 per cent, and procurement climbed 20 per cent, even as its sales and business development intake declined 5 per cent.
The BPO and ITES sector expanded primarily through specialised business functions. Customer success, service, and operations hiring remained flat at zero per cent. 
In contrast, finance and accounting roles surged 84 per cent, sales and business development increased 43 per cent, and software engineering and QA grew 42 per cent.
In technology, IT and software services grew 5 per cent, but AI and machine learning positions rose 32 per cent, while Global Capability Centres increased recruitment by 18 per cent. Broad software engineering and QA across all sectors rose 1 per cent.
Across experience brackets, senior hiring expanded the fastest, with both the 13 to 16 years and over 16 years categories rising 22 per cent. Fresher hiring grew 15 per cent. 
Geographically, Hyderabad led metros with 15 per cent growth, while Gujarat dominated emerging markets, led by Gandhinagar at 48 per cent, Surat at 36 per cent, Vadodara at 30 per cent, and Ahmedabad at 23 per cent. (ANI)
